findings.evidence: Lines 59 and 91 introduce `Module.Free` solely to choose a basis for the direct-sum proof; Mathlib provides `Module.Projective.of_free` at `Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Projective.lean:161`, confirming freeness is strictly the stronger interface.
findings.fix: State both one-sided results under `[Module.Projective K W]`/`[Module.Projective K V]`, proving them via a free-module splitting; the existing free cases then follow from `Module.Projective.of_free`.
findings.issue: `IsSemisimple.rTensor` requires `[Module.Free K W]`, and `IsSemisimple.lTensor` analogously requires freeness of `V`, although projective modules are direct summands of free modules and tensoring preserves that splitting.

summary: The one-sided semisimplicity API is unnecessarily restricted to free tensor factors; the natural hypothesis is projectivity.
